episode.subject: Florida manatees nuzzling
episode.title: How she says hello
episode.body:
When she came back, I went towards her very slowly. I could see the pale marks across her back.

She put her nose against mine. I barely pressed.

She asked whether I had forgotten her.

I said of course not.

She pushed harder.

I had been remembering all the ways I might hurt her. I had forgotten how firmly she liked to say hello.

I pushed back. She moved a little.

Then she came at me again.

proposals.visibleScene: Two adult-sized manatees touch noses. Left animal faces right, near animal faces away and left. Pale parallel scars cross near animal back. Faces and contact are recognizable through considerable blue water haze; no acute wound shown.
proposals.fictionBoundary: Nellie is left animal; scarred foreground animal is fictional adult female acquaintance. Sex is not established by image. Return, prior familiarity, dialogue, pressure, fear of causing pain, pushing back and renewed approach are fiction. FWS establishes nuzzling and boat-propeller scars, not the encounter history or current pain.
proposals.continuity: Append after current thirteen Nellie episodes. Adult companion is not the calf from Her turn. Preserve Nellie own body, avatar, home and all previous wording. Companion gains scars here, not Nellie. This episode does not date the accident, invent a rescue or imply complete recovery. Exact source Crystal River matches canon home.
proposals.authorReview: The visible contact permits a physical answer to misplaced caution. The desired turn is fear of hurting an old friend giving way to a familiar greeting. Similarity to Her turn must be judged candidly: both use pushing, but the prior scene is a mother making a calf feel effective; here the adult companion refuses excessive caution and Nellie participates more fully. Image haze is the principal risk; reject if the pair does not meet the visual bar.
proposals.biologyEvidence: Primary FWS caption confirms nuzzling and propeller scars. Independently opened USGS Manatee Scars page describes recognizable scars from non-fatal boat encounters and entanglements. No general medical prognosis claimed.
